name: Extinct Orders
summary: Factions that shaped the world and ended. Their ruins, seals, and unfinished works are adventure sites; their ideas never quite died — they evolved into the factions of today.

orders.name: The Colleges of the Weave
orders.summary: The teaching institutions of high magic. Seven great colleges taught the song as craft; their ruins still hum in the Ashlands.

history.event: Ith-belen binds the first thread; within a decade the first college opens its doors.
The colleges raise Velkash on the Silk; their woven bridges stand where masons would have failed.
The Bound Storms: the colleges' proudest working plants the first seed of common fear.
The Sundering destroys four colleges outright; three seal themselves and are never heard from again.

orders.legacy: Sealed colleges may still hold Weavers — or something wearing them. The Censer's archive-quarter is built on a college's foundation.

orders.name: The High Concord
orders.ended: 1 Sun (winter) — dissolved into the First Censer
orders.summary: The Weavers' ruling conclave, formed to contain the song after hubris became policy. It contained nothing, but its wardens survived to swear the Censer's oath.

history.event: Formed by moderates horrified by the Bound Storms; given power to sanction or forbid any working.
Refuses Ithyn's push to bind the whole song; Ithyn's exile splits the Concord's soul.
Leads the Silent War against the Unbinding faction — and wins every battle while losing the world.
Its own hardliners speak the Song Unbinding at the Stone Crown, believing controlled unbinding safer than Ithyn's heirs' chaos.
Survivors dissolve the Concord and swear the First Censer's oath in Velkash's broken thread-quarter.

orders.legacy: The Censer is the High Concord's ghost — same fear, new name. Its seal (a ring of nine threads) survives in the Nine Ashes' voting stones.

orders.name: The Unbinding Faction
orders.ended: 1,201 CoW — destroyed by its own victory
orders.summary: Ithyn's heirs, who believed the song belonged to no institution. They won the Silent War, completed the Song Unbinding, and were annihilated by what they unleashed.

history.event: A dozen exiled acolytes take the name Unbinding and begin teaching in secret.
Fight the Silent War with stolen workings; lose cities, gain converts.
Hardliners among the High Concord steal the Unbinding's texts — the faction's own words doom the world.
The Sundering. A third die, a third go mad, a third walk silent into the Quiet. The faction ends as a name on Censer watchlists.

orders.legacy: The Rememberers claim their memory; the Censer claims their guilt. Both are half right. The 'silent ones' who walked into the Quiet may be the faction's last members — still singing.

orders.name: The First Whisperers
orders.summary: Ithyn's first dozen students, taught the Unbinding before Ithyn's exile. Some repented into the High Concord's service; some founded the Unbinding; one is said to have walked into the Quiet alive and on purpose.

history.event: Ithyn teaches twelve acolytes the whole song, believing knowledge shared cannot be hoarded.
Ithyn's exile scatters them: four repent and join the Concord's wardens, seven found the Unbinding, one — Beleth the Quiet-Walker — vanishes toward the Ashlands.
The last repentant Whisperer — a founding warden of the First Censer — dies in service; the confession is sealed in the archive's deepest vault.

orders.legacy: Beleth's fate is unwritten history. If she lived, her descendants — mortal or otherwise — would be 2,000 years old and remember everything.

orders.name: The Nine Hearths
orders.founded: ~2,100 AS, at the First Battle of the Sky
orders.summary: The mortal alliance of the god-war: nine river-tribes who swore mutual shelter while immortal armies burned the sky. The only authority that functioned through the War of Heaven's Edge.

history.event: At the First Battle of the Sky, nine hearth-fires are lit in one vale; each tribe vows shelter to any who flee the divine war, friend or stranger.
Keep neutral ways and refugee roads through the war; bury the dead of both immortal armies in shared ground no god may claim.
Survive the Withdrawal as the continent's only working authority — roads kept, granaries sealed, oaths intact.
As the Weavers rise, hearth authority fades. The last moot dissolves the Compact voluntarily, gifting its refugee roads to the new kingdoms.

orders.legacy: The King's Road follows their refugee roads. 'Hearth-right' — shelter for any who ask — survives as folk custom across the Crownlands. The salt-and-harvest council's round table echoes the hearth-moot.

orders.name: Karvess, the Glass Kingdom
orders.summary: The greatest glass city-state of the southern Concord, founded by weavers who left Velkash over craft disputes. Now the Ruin of Karvess — the largest standing ruin in the Ashlands.

history.event: The Glass Schism: master weavers who scorn silk leave Velkash to weave light itself; Karvess raises towers of woven glass over the southern plain.
Height of the kingdom: light-works banish night across the Ashlands; even Velkash buys Karvess glass.
Joins the High Concord reluctantly; its weavers favor binding over unbinding and oppose the Silent War on both sides.
The Rent passes directly beneath the city; Karvess vitrifies in a single hour — towers, people, and fountains turned to glass together.
Formally counted among the Falling Kingdoms. Survivors scatter south; some say hollowborn Rememberers count Karvess among their ancestors.

orders.legacy: The Ruin of Karvess hums on quiet nights. The Censer forbids all expeditions; the Reeve wants one mounted. What the glass remembers, no one has dared ask.

orders.name: House Dellet
orders.founded: ~150 Si, ennobled after the first continental purge
orders.ended: ~460 Si — extinguished by its own choice
orders.summary: The Censer's ennobled hunters. Granted title and land for every Glimmerborn delivered, they became the purge's face — and its most willing hands.

history.event: House Dellet elevated to nobility after delivering seventeen Glimmerborn in a single season — a record the Nine Ashes still cite.
Lead the Great Collection's field work. 'The Dellets are coming' becomes a threat parents hush children with.
The heir, Sella Dellet, is born Glimmerborn. The house faces the choice its whole history was built on: blood or oath.
Chooses the oath. Surrenders Sella to the Censer, seals the house line, and cedes its lands to the order. No Dellet is recorded again.

orders.legacy: The Dellet estate is now the Censer Quarter's eastern wall. 'Dellet's choice' is proverbial for duty over love — and what became of Sella is the order's most quietly guarded question.

orders.name: Solmere, the Bright Kingdom
orders.summary: The kingdom that tried to restore the golden age in a generation. Its fall is the Censer's favorite cautionary tale — and the legal foundation of the order's modern warrant.

history.event: Founded on the Thresher's Vale's south bank by followers of a Solvane revival movement preaching that the sun god's silence could be ended by worthy works.
Solmere's courts quietly employ hedge-casters: the Glimmer taxed, licensed, and taught — a controlled return of magic, generations before the Waking.
Proclaims the Second Dawn: public workings, a reopened college, Old Weaver studied openly. Refugees of fear flee the Crownlands for Solmere's promise.
The Backfiring: a civic working meant to bless the harvest tears a pocket of Quiet beneath the capital. The city of Solmere is now a silence-zone inside the Crownlands.
The Censer arrives to 'help'. The shattered Crownlands sign the Accords granting the order its modern warrant — the law the Reeve's court now chafes against.

orders.legacy: Every Censer argument ends with 'remember Solmere'. The silence-zone is off-limits by treaty; some Veil-Wardens believe the working still runs beneath it, waiting to finish what it started.
